subject: Apollo — run-rate modeling, safety buffer, and emergency fallback
messages:
From: Avery Stone <avery.stone@apolloai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing ask for Q1 run-rate + fallback plan

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the chat yesterday. We're trying to lock down numbers for our Q1 commitment and need a deal-level sizing sheet that ties directly to our desired SLOs and an emergency fallback plan. High-level ask:

- Baseline expected traffic: 6M tokens/day (evenly spread)
- Peak window: 15-minute peak expected to reach ~420 tokens/sec system-wide
- Typical request footprint: median 320 tokens per request, 95th ~1,100 tokens (long form summarization flows)
- Target latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end < 1.2s for generation-only calls (we accept slightly higher tail if we keep 99th < 2.8s)

Can you provide:
1) Recommended dedicated capacity (GPU count + instance type) for a committed run-rate that meets the SLO with a safety buffer (headroom % and rationale)
2) A cheaper emergency fallback configuration (quantized variant, smaller model, or region failover) and estimated QoS impact
3) Any ops constraints / lead times we should factor into procurement and rollout

We're aiming to sign by mid-Jan, so a short, actionable doc is ideal. I've attached a simple traffic CSV and the procurement contact (procurement@apolloai.com).

Thanks,
Avery
Director, Product
Apollo AI

Attachments: Apollo_traffic_Q1.csv (CSV)

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Apollo's ask. Key numbers: baseline 6M tokens/day, 15-min peak ~420 tps system-wide, median req ~320 tokens, 95th ~1.1k tokens. Target SLO 95p <1.2s.

Two quick asks:
- Can you sketch 2 scenarios: "Commit" (hard reserved capacity to hit SLO with 30% headroom) and "Commit + Burst" (reserved baseline + burst pool + fallback model)
- Include per-GPU throughput assumptions (we should call out model variant and quantization) and an ops lead-time estimate (procurement / cluster prep / region failover)

I'll consolidate into a one-pager to send to Avery.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-27T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing ask for Q1 run-rate + fallback plan

Hannah / team — ran numbers and attached a compact calc spreadsheet (Apollo_MRG_capacity_calc.xlsx). Summary below; I tried to keep conservative assumptions explicit so Apollo can make a tradeoff.

Assumptions / baseline
- Chosen model: OSS-L3-70B-opt (float16 runtime, optimized kernels) for primary path. Fallback variant: OSS-L3-70B-8bit (int8/quant) or OSS-L3-13B for cheaper fallback.
- Avg tokens per request: use median 320 for steady-state; for peak planning use 95th 1,100 tokens for tail capacity math.
- Measured per-worker throughput (H100, optimized runtime):
  - Steady small context (<=512): ~2,400 tokens/sec per GPU (batching active)
  - Mixed long context (avg 320, but lots of 1.1k): effective sustained ~1,200 tokens/sec per GPU when accounting for KV/cache and tail variance
- Latency mapping (single GPU, 95p): at 1,200 tps on model path -> ~550ms generation latency; added networking / pre/post = ~750-850ms end-to-end.

Scenario A — Commit (30% headroom target)
- Peak requirement calc: Apollo peak 420 tps system-wide * safety multiplier for long-requests = ~700 tokens/sec effective demand (weighted for long tails).
- Target capacity with 30% headroom => required capacity = 700 * 1.3 = 910 tokens/sec equivalent.
- Using conservative per-GPU sustained 1,200 tps => GPUs required = ceil(910 / 1,200) = 1 GPU. (Note: this is "per-region" math; we'll provision multi-AZ redundancy and spread inference for latency.)
- Practical recommendation: 3 x H100-equivalent GPUs reserved across 2 AZs. Rationale: single-GPU math looks small because of the optimistic per-GPU throughput; we need redundancy, maintenance, and regional failover. 3 GPUs provides ~3,600 tps theoretical, which gives ~4x headroom vs calculated run-rate and allows CANARY/rolling restarts.

Scenario B — Commit + Burst (baseline + burst pool)
- Baseline: reserve 2 x H100 GPUs (sustained ~2,400 tps) to handle steady plus short spikes comfortably.
- Burst pool: add 6 burst GPUs in shared pool (hot-standby) that you can spin up or route to in 1–3 minutes; these can be on cheaper instances or pre-warmed.
- Fallback model: L3-70B-8bit provides ~1.8x per-GPU throughput in tests (so ~2,200 tps effective) but increases hallucination risk slightly; expected 95p latency increases by ~20–40% for long-context requests.

Ops notes / lead times
- Procurement + dedicated pool setup: 3–6 weeks (depends on region availability).
- Pre-warm strategy: pre-load KV/cache on 2 baseline GPUs; burst pool kept at warm checkpoint state => reduces cold-start tail by ~400–900ms.
- Networking: enable cross-AZ routing and a simple fallback policy to force traffic to quantized variant when 95p latency breaches 1.2s for >30s.

Risks & mitigations
- Long-tail requests dominate token volume; recommend a prefix-caching policy and request size caps in client SDK to blunt pathological single-request spikes.
- If Apollo wants a strict 99.9% SLA on tail, we'd need to double the reserved baseline or add a regional sibling cluster.

I'll attach the calc and a short set of sensitivity scenarios (cache efficacy + burst pool sizes). Happy to walk through the sheet.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Apollo_MRG_capacity_calc.xlsx (XLSX)

Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing ask for Q1 run-rate + fallback plan

Quick operational addenda from my side:

1) Caching & request shaping: If we can get Apollo to add a 1–2 second client-side cache for repeated prompts and a 65% hit-rate on short reuse flows, effective token load drops by ~25–30%. That materially reduces needed burst capacity.

2) Deployment topology: recommend split traffic by region and use Smart Routing policy: baseline traffic stays in primary us-west region; burst/fallback traffic can route to us-east cheaper pool to avoid contention during spikes.

3) Observability hooks: provide a small eval set of 200 prompts (Apollo-specific) to run nightly to detect quality regressions if we switch to quantized fallback. We'll tie quality regression alerts to auto-rollbacks.

4) Procurement timing: if they need contractual language on instance type and on-call response windows, we should include a standard addendum (I can share language). Lead time remains ~3–6 weeks; recommend starting paperwork this week to hit mid-Jan sign.

Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Avery Stone <avery.stone@apolloai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, procurement@apolloai.com

Subject: Apollo — run-rate modeling, safety buffer, and emergency fallback

Avery — thanks for the patience. Short summary and next steps below (attaching PO template for procurement).

Executive summary (one paragraph)
We recommend a reserved baseline of 2 H100-class GPUs for Q1 to cover steady-state and shorter spikes, with a burst pool of 6 additional GPUs (hot-standby) and a quantized fallback path (L3-70B-8bit or L3-13B) for emergency overflow. This hybrid gives expected 95p latency ~0.8–1.1s on primary path, and preserves application availability under >2x spike events while keeping committed spend efficient.

Concrete next steps
1) Review the attached PO_template.pdf with procurement (procurement@apolloai.com) — we filled the instance type and lead-time placeholders.
2) If you agree to the hybrid proposal, we will:
   - Lock baseline reservation (2 GPUs) + reserve the burst pool capacity (6 GPUs idle)
   - Pre-warm KV/cache on 2 baseline GPUs and configure Smart Routing + fallback rules
   - Run the 200-prompt nightly eval for 72 hours against their dataset to baseline quality on quantized fallback
3) Timeline: commit and procurement sign by Jan 12 -> infra ready & end-to-end tests by Feb 2 (roughly 3 weeks from contract)

Tradeoffs & readouts
- Cost: baseline reservation + burst pool is ~40% cheaper than reserving 8 dedicated GPUs; we presented both numbers in the spreadsheet.
- Quality: fallback quantized model reduces per-token cost but will increase hallucination risk slightly for long-context prompts; monitoring + auto-rollbacks mitigate most practical issues.

I'll schedule a 30-min call for early next week to review the calc with you and procurement if that works.

Cheers,
Hannah
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: PO_template.pdf (PDF)
